claim: EphA7 is a juxtacrine signaling receptor expressed on myocytes during embryonic and fetal myogenesis.
source: We show that EphA7, a juxtacrine signaling receptor, is expressed on myocytes during embryonic and fetal myogenesis and on nascent myofibers during muscle regeneration in vivo.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 1-3.

claim: EphA7 is expressed on nascent myofibers during muscle regeneration in vivo.
source: We show that EphA7, a juxtacrine signaling receptor, is expressed on myocytes during embryonic and fetal myogenesis and on nascent myofibers during muscle regeneration in vivo.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 1 showing EphA7 expression during muscle regeneration timecourse.

claim: In EphA7-/- mice, hindlimb muscles possess fewer myofibers at birth.
source: In EphA7-/- mice, hindlimb muscles possess fewer myofibers at birth, and those myofibers are reduced in size and have fewer myonuclei and reduced overall numbers of precursor cells throughout postnatal life.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Myofibers in EphA7-/- mice are reduced in size.
source: In EphA7-/- mice, hindlimb muscles possess fewer myofibers at birth, and those myofibers are reduced in size and have fewer myonuclei and reduced overall numbers of precursor cells throughout postnatal life.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Myofibers in EphA7-/- mice have fewer myonuclei.
source: In EphA7-/- mice, hindlimb muscles possess fewer myofibers at birth, and those myofibers are reduced in size and have fewer myonuclei and reduced overall numbers of precursor cells throughout postnatal life.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: EphA7-/- mice have reduced overall numbers of precursor cells throughout postnatal life.
source: In EphA7-/- mice, hindlimb muscles possess fewer myofibers at birth, and those myofibers are reduced in size and have fewer myonuclei and reduced overall numbers of precursor cells throughout postnatal life.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Adult EphA7-/- mice have reduced numbers of satellite cells.
source: Adult EphA7-/- mice have reduced numbers of satellite cells and exhibit delayed and protracted muscle regeneration, and satellite cell-derived myogenic cells from EphA7-/- mice are delayed in their expression of differentiation markers in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Adult EphA7-/- mice exhibit delayed and protracted muscle regeneration.
source: Adult EphA7-/- mice have reduced numbers of satellite cells and exhibit delayed and protracted muscle regeneration, and satellite cell-derived myogenic cells from EphA7-/- mice are delayed in their expression of differentiation markers in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 5 showing persistence of eMyHC expression and delayed hypertrophy.

claim: Satellite cell-derived myogenic cells from EphA7-/- mice are delayed in their expression of differentiation markers in vitro.
source: Adult EphA7-/- mice have reduced numbers of satellite cells and exhibit delayed and protracted muscle regeneration, and satellite cell-derived myogenic cells from EphA7-/- mice are delayed in their expression of differentiation markers in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 6 showing reduced myogenin expression in EphA7-/- cells.

claim: Exogenous EphA7 extracellular domain will rescue the null phenotype in vitro.
source: Exogenous EphA7 extracellular domain will rescue the null phenotype in vitro, and will also enhance commitment to differentiation in WT cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 7 showing rescue of differentiation in EphA7-/- cells exposed to EphA7-Fc.

claim: Exogenous EphA7 extracellular domain will enhance commitment to differentiation in WT cells.
source: Exogenous EphA7 extracellular domain will rescue the null phenotype in vitro, and will also enhance commitment to differentiation in WT cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by data in Figure 7 showing enhanced differentiation in WT cells exposed to EphA7-Fc.

claim: EphA7 expression on differentiated myocytes promotes commitment of adjacent myoblasts to terminal differentiation.
source: We propose a model in which EphA7 expression on differentiated myocytes promotes commitment of adjacent myoblasts to terminal differentiation.
evidence: This is the proposed model based on the experimental findings, supported by data showing non-cell-autonomous effects and rescue with exogenous EphA7 ectodomain.

claim: The sartorius muscle in humans can be approximately 60 cm long.
source: in humans, the sartorius muscle can be ~60 cm long, with individual muscle fibers longer than 20 cm (Harris et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Harris et al., 2005.

claim: Individual muscle fibers in the human sartorius muscle can be longer than 20 cm.
source: in humans, the sartorius muscle can be ~60 cm long, with individual muscle fibers longer than 20 cm (Harris et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Harris et al., 2005.

claim: Myofibers are generated by the fusion of terminally postmitotic myocytes.
source: Myofibers are generated by the fusion of terminally postmitotic myocytes, which differentiate from proliferation-competent myoblasts.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field of muscle biology.

claim: Myocytes differentiate from proliferation-competent myoblasts.
source: Myofibers are generated by the fusion of terminally postmitotic myocytes, which differentiate from proliferation-competent myoblasts.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field of muscle biology.

claim: Sparse plating of myogenic cells in vitro delays myogenic differentiation.
source: It is a common observation that sparse plating of myogenic cells in vitro delays myogenic differentiation, while cells cultured at higher confluence exhibit a much higher degree of differentiation regardless of pro-mitogenic conditions such as high serum.
evidence: This is described as a common observation in the field, representing established knowledge.

claim: Cells cultured at higher confluence exhibit a much higher degree of differentiation regardless of pro-mitogenic conditions such as high serum.
source: It is a common observation that sparse plating of myogenic cells in vitro delays myogenic differentiation, while cells cultured at higher confluence exhibit a much higher degree of differentiation regardless of pro-mitogenic conditions such as high serum.
evidence: This is described as a common observation in the field, representing established knowledge.

claim: Single mesoderm cells or aggregates of less than 100 mesoderm cells will not express MyoD and differentiate into muscle even under conditions that promote myogenesis.
source: He found that single mesoderm cells or aggregates of less than 100 mesoderm cells will not express MyoD and differentiate into muscle even under conditions that promote myogenesis, while aggregates of 100 or more cells would differentiate efficiently (Gurdon et al., 1993)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Gurdon et al., 1993.

claim: Aggregates of 100 or more mesoderm cells would differentiate efficiently.
source: He found that single mesoderm cells or aggregates of less than 100 mesoderm cells will not express MyoD and differentiate into muscle even under conditions that promote myogenesis, while aggregates of 100 or more cells would differentiate efficiently (Gurdon et al., 1993)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Gurdon et al., 1993.

claim: N-cadherin is responsible for at least a portion of the community effect in muscle development.
source: later experiments showed that the homotypic cell-cell adhesion molecule N-cadherin is responsible for at least a portion of this effect (Holt et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Holt et al., 1994.

claim: A minimum of 30–40 cells is required for myogenic differentiation in mouse.
source: Similar studies in mouse suggested that a minimum of 30–40 cells is required for myogenic differentiation (Cossu et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cossu et al., 1995.

claim: Ephs are a family of receptor tyrosine kinases that act via juxtacrine interactions with cells presenting their ligands (ephrins).
source: Ephs are a family of receptor tyrosine kinases that act via juxtacrine interactions with cells presenting their ligands (ephrins) to modify cell motility, assortment, proliferation, differentiation, and survival in multiple tissue types (Klein, 2010; Klein, 2012; Kania and Klein, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Klein, 2010; Klein, 2012; Kania and Klein, 2016.

claim: Eph:ephrin interactions modify cell motility, assortment, proliferation, differentiation, and survival in multiple tissue types.
source: Ephs are a family of receptor tyrosine kinases that act via juxtacrine interactions with cells presenting their ligands (ephrins) to modify cell motility, assortment, proliferation, differentiation, and survival in multiple tissue types (Klein, 2010; Klein, 2012; Kania and Klein, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Klein, 2010; Klein, 2012; Kania and Klein, 2016.

claim: EphA7 is absent during muscle homeostasis.
source: Our initial observations in an expression screen for Eph/ephrins in the context of adult skeletal muscle regeneration suggested that EphA7, while absent during muscle homeostasis, is transiently upregulated by regenerating myofibers in vivo after a barium chloride (BaCl2) injury (Stark et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Stark et al., 2011 and by data in Figure 1 showing no EphA7 expression in uninjured muscle.

claim: EphA7 is transiently upregulated by regenerating myofibers in vivo after a barium chloride (BaCl2) injury.
source: Our initial observations in an expression screen for Eph/ephrins in the context of adult skeletal muscle regeneration suggested that EphA7, while absent during muscle homeostasis, is transiently upregulated by regenerating myofibers in vivo after a barium chloride (BaCl2) injury (Stark et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Stark et al., 2011 and by data in Figure 1 showing EphA7 expression during regeneration.

claim: EphA7 protein was consistently expressed by nascent myofibers at all timepoints examined during regeneration.
source: We noted that EphA7 protein was consistently expressed by nascent myofibers at all timepoints examined, and that as muscle regeneration was resolved, muscle fiber caliber increased, and eMyHC expression was lost, EphA7 expression was also extinguished (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1.

claim: As muscle regeneration was resolved, muscle fiber caliber increased, and eMyHC expression was lost, EphA7 expression was also extinguished.
source: We noted that EphA7 protein was consistently expressed by nascent myofibers at all timepoints examined, and that as muscle regeneration was resolved, muscle fiber caliber increased, and eMyHC expression was lost, EphA7 expression was also extinguished (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Full-length EphA7 is the most abundant isoform expressed during muscle regeneration.
source: We found that full-length EphA7 is the most abundant isoform expressed during muscle regeneration, although both truncated isoforms were also detected at varying levels. (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both truncated isoforms of EphA7 were also detected at varying levels during muscle regeneration.
source: We found that full-length EphA7 is the most abundant isoform expressed during muscle regeneration, although both truncated isoforms were also detected at varying levels. (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of EphA7 was first detected on relatively few satellite cells at 48 hours after isolation when cultured in association with their host myofiber.
source: When satellite cells were isolated and cultured in association with their host myofiber, expression of EphA7 was first detected on relatively few cells at 48 hours after isolation, but was seen on the majority of satellite cells by 96 hours in culture (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: EphA7 was seen on the majority of satellite cells by 96 hours in culture when cultured in association with their host myofiber.
source: When satellite cells were isolated and cultured in association with their host myofiber, expression of EphA7 was first detected on relatively few cells at 48 hours after isolation, but was seen on the majority of satellite cells by 96 hours in culture (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In monoculture, EphA7 expression is detectable only in a few dispersed cells when they are initially plated under low serum conditions.
source: In monoculture, EphA7 expression is detectable only in a few dispersed cells when they are initially plated under low serum conditions (Figure 2B), but one day later it is present in individual cells or more often groups of cells in close association with one another and/or with bipolar morphology suggesting differentiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: One day after plating in low serum, EphA7 is present in individual cells or more often groups of cells in close association with one another and/or with bipolar morphology suggesting differentiation.
source: In monoculture, EphA7 expression is detectable only in a few dispersed cells when they are initially plated under low serum conditions (Figure 2B), but one day later it is present in individual cells or more often groups of cells in close association with one another and/or with bipolar morphology suggesting differentiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: After three days in low serum, the majority of cells are EphA7+.
source: After three days in low serum, the majority of cells are EphA7+.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Expression of EphA7 and Pax7 are mutually exclusive.
source: At all timepoints tested we saw that expression of EphA7 and Pax7 are mutually exclusive, while EphA7 and myogenin are uniformly coexpressed, suggesting that EphA7 expression is restricted to committed myocytes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: EphA7 and myogenin are uniformly coexpressed.
source: At all timepoints tested we saw that expression of EphA7 and Pax7 are mutually exclusive, while EphA7 and myogenin are uniformly coexpressed, suggesting that EphA7 expression is restricted to committed myocytes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: EphA7 expression is restricted to committed myocytes.
source: At all timepoints tested we saw that expression of EphA7 and Pax7 are mutually exclusive, while EphA7 and myogenin are uniformly coexpressed, suggesting that EphA7 expression is restricted to committed myocytes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is inferred from the mutually exclusive expression with Pax7 and uniform coexpression with myogenin, as shown in Figure 2C.

claim: MyoD is present in a subset of EphA7+ cells, presumably differentiated myocytes.
source: MyoD, which is expressed by both proliferating and differentiating myogenic cells, is present in a subset of EphA7+ cells, presumably differentiated myocytes.
evidence: This statement is based on immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2C and inference about cell identity.

claim: EphA7 mRNA is present by e11.5.
source: Prior work suggests that EphA7 mRNA is present by e11.5 (Alonso-Martin et al., 2016), when myogenic differentiation in the somites and limb buds will have already begun.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Alonso-Martin et al., 2016.

claim: At e11.5, EphA7 protein staining was observed in the dermomyotome on the surface of cells also expressing MyoD.
source: At e11.5, we observed EphA7 protein staining in the dermomyotome on the surface of cells also expressing MyoD (Figure 3A), although populations of MyoD+ cells at the dorsomedial lip (which will migrate under the dermomyotome then differentiate to form the primary myotome) and the ventrolateral lip (which will migrate to the limb buds then differentiate to form the limb musculature) do not express EphA7.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Populations of MyoD+ cells at the dorsomedial lip do not express EphA7 at e11.5.
source: At e11.5, we observed EphA7 protein staining in the dermomyotome on the surface of cells also expressing MyoD (Figure 3A), although populations of MyoD+ cells at the dorsomedial lip (which will migrate under the dermomyotome then differentiate to form the primary myotome) and the ventrolateral lip (which will migrate to the limb buds then differentiate to form the limb musculature) do not express EphA7.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Populations of MyoD+ cells at the ventrolateral lip do not express EphA7 at e11.5.
source: At e11.5, we observed EphA7 protein staining in the dermomyotome on the surface of cells also expressing MyoD (Figure 3A), although populations of MyoD+ cells at the dorsomedial lip (which will migrate under the dermomyotome then differentiate to form the primary myotome) and the ventrolateral lip (which will migrate to the limb buds then differentiate to form the limb musculature) do not express EphA7.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: When costained for myogenin in equivalent sections at e11.5, EphA7+ cells in the somite all express myogenin.
source: When costained for myogenin in equivalent sections, EphA7+ cells in the somite all express myogenin, indicating that they have committed to differentiation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In oblique sections through the developing somites at e11.5, the most recently-differentiated cells express myogenin but not yet EphA7.
source: This can be more easily noted in oblique sections through the developing somites, in which mononuclear, differentiated primary myotome fibers can be viewed from end to end; in these sections we see that the most recently-differentiated cells express myogenin but not yet EphA7 (arrow).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: EphA7 is expressed in all myosin heavy chain (MyHC)-expressing differentiated myocytes in the somite at e11.5.
source: Finally, EphA7 is expressed in all myosin heavy chain (MyHC)-expressing differentiated myocytes in the somite (Figure 3C).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: By e15.5, EphA7 is expressed on differentiated, myogenin+/MyHC+ myocytes and myofibers in muscles of forelimbs.
source: By e15.5, we observe EphA7 expression on differentiated, myogenin+/MyHC+ myocytes and myofibers in muscles of forelimbs (Figure 3D) and trunk (diaphragm and body wall) (Figure 3E) as well.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: By e15.5, EphA7 is expressed on differentiated, myogenin+/MyHC+ myocytes and myofibers in trunk muscles (diaphragm and body wall).
source: By e15.5, we observe EphA7 expression on differentiated, myogenin+/MyHC+ myocytes and myofibers in muscles of forelimbs (Figure 3D) and trunk (diaphragm and body wall) (Figure 3E) as well.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The EphA7-/- mouse strain has multiple nonlethal defects in the central nervous system.
source: This strain has multiple nonlethal defects in the central nervous system (Rashid et al., 2005; Clifford et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2016) but no skeletal muscle phenotype has been described.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rashid et al., 2005; Clifford et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2016.

claim: No skeletal muscle phenotype has been described for the EphA7-/- mouse strain prior to this study.
source: This strain has multiple nonlethal defects in the central nervous system (Rashid et al., 2005; Clifford et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2016) but no skeletal muscle phenotype has been described.
evidence: This statement is based on the absence of prior reports in the literature.

claim: EphA7-/- mice are smaller than WT littermates at birth.
source: We noted that EphA7-/- mice are smaller than WT littermates at birth, and hindlimb muscle wet weight is reduced in adult mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Hindlimb muscle wet weight is reduced in adult EphA7-/- mice.
source: We noted that EphA7-/- mice are smaller than WT littermates at birth, and hindlimb muscle wet weight is reduced in adult mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The decrease in muscle mass in EphA7-/- mice appears to be due to both a reduction in myofiber number and in myofiber size.
source: The decrease appears to be due to both a reduction in myofiber number and in myofiber size (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: EphA7-/- muscles initially possess fewer nascent (embryonic myosin heavy chain+) myofibers early in regeneration than WT (3 dpi).
source: After acute injury, EphA7-/- muscles initially possess fewer nascent (embryonic myosin heavy chain+) myofibers early in regeneration than WT (3 dpi).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At later time points eMyHC expression persists in EphA7-/- muscles when it has become extinguished in favor of adult isoforms in WT (7–10 dpi).
source: At later time points eMyHC expression persists in EphA7-/- muscles when it has become extinguished in favor of adult isoforms in WT (7–10 dpi).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: At 10 dpi, some eMyHC+ myofiber profiles in regenerated EphA7-/- muscle could be identified as unfused myocytes or small, mononucleated myofibers lacking a basal lamina.
source: On closer examination (Figure 5B–C), some eMyHC+ myofiber profiles in regenerated EphA7-/- muscle could be identified as unfused myocytes or small, mononucleated myofibers lacking a basal lamina.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 5B-C.

claim: Muscle fiber diameter had returned to baseline by 28 days in both WT and EphA7-/- genotypes.
source: While muscle fiber diameter had returned to baseline by 28 days in both genotypes, hypertrophy was delayed in the EphA7-/- muscles both initially (between 5 and 10 dpi) and later when WT fiber diameter had nearly recovered (14 dpi) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Hypertrophy was delayed in the EphA7-/- muscles both initially (between 5 and 10 dpi) and later when WT fiber diameter had nearly recovered (14 dpi).
source: While muscle fiber diameter had returned to baseline by 28 days in both genotypes, hypertrophy was delayed in the EphA7-/- muscles both initially (between 5 and 10 dpi) and later when WT fiber diameter had nearly recovered (14 dpi) (Figure 5D).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cell proliferation was not significantly different between WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells cultured on their host myofibers at 48 hours after isolation.
source: We noted that while cell proliferation and upregulation of MyoD were not significantly different between WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells cultured on their host myofibers at 48 hours after myofibers (Figure 6A–B), upregulation of myogenin expression was greatly decreased in EphA7-/- satellite cells at 96 hours (Figure 6C).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Upregulation of MyoD was not significantly different between WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells cultured on their host myofibers at 48 hours after isolation.
source: We noted that while cell proliferation and upregulation of MyoD were not significantly different between WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells cultured on their host myofibers at 48 hours after myofibers (Figure 6A–B), upregulation of myogenin expression was greatly decreased in EphA7-/- satellite cells at 96 hours (Figure 6C).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Upregulation of myogenin expression was greatly decreased in EphA7-/- satellite cells at 96 hours when cultured on their host myofibers.
source: We noted that while cell proliferation and upregulation of MyoD were not significantly different between WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells cultured on their host myofibers at 48 hours after myofibers (Figure 6A–B), upregulation of myogenin expression was greatly decreased in EphA7-/- satellite cells at 96 hours (Figure 6C).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The fraction of satellite cells in monoculture expressing Pax7 did not differ between WT and EphA7-/- cells.
source: Similarly, the fraction of satellite cells in monoculture expressing of Pax7, proliferating (not shown), and expressing MyoD (Figure 6D) did not differ between WT and EphA7-/- cells, but expression of myogenin was significantly decreased (Figure 6E).
evidence: This statement is based on quantitative analysis of immunocytochemistry data.

claim: The fraction of satellite cells in monoculture expressing MyoD did not differ between WT and EphA7-/- cells.
source: Similarly, the fraction of satellite cells in monoculture expressing of Pax7, proliferating (not shown), and expressing MyoD (Figure 6D) did not differ between WT and EphA7-/- cells, but expression of myogenin was significantly decreased (Figure 6E).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Expression of myogenin was significantly decreased in EphA7-/- satellite cells in monoculture.
source: Similarly, the fraction of satellite cells in monoculture expressing of Pax7, proliferating (not shown), and expressing MyoD (Figure 6D) did not differ between WT and EphA7-/- cells, but expression of myogenin was significantly decreased (Figure 6E).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: EphA7 is not expressed by FAPs either during homeostasis or injury.
source: EphA7 is not expressed by FAPS either during homeostasis or injury (based on bulk RNA-seq, Joe et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Joe et al., 2010.

claim: 12 hours of exposure to EphA7-Fc rescued differentiation of EphA7-/- cells to WT levels.
source: We found that even at the earliest time assayed (12 hours after plating), the fraction of EphA7-/- cells on EphA7-Fc scoring positive for myogenin was equivalent to that of WT cells on laminin, while WT cells on EphA7-Fc differentiated to a greater extent than WT cells on laminin alone (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: WT cells on EphA7-Fc differentiated to a greater extent than WT cells on laminin alone.
source: We found that even at the earliest time assayed (12 hours after plating), the fraction of EphA7-/- cells on EphA7-Fc scoring positive for myogenin was equivalent to that of WT cells on laminin, while WT cells on EphA7-Fc differentiated to a greater extent than WT cells on laminin alone (Figure 7A).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: By 48 hours of exposure, EphA7-/- cells stimulated with EphA7-Fc showed myogenin expression and differentiated morphologies indistinguishable from WT.
source: These results were consistent over the course of the assay, and by 48 hours of exposure EphA7-/- cells stimulated with EphA7-Fc showed myogenin expression and differentiated morphologies indistinguishable from WT (Figure 7B).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: EphA7 acts non-cell-autonomously as a myocyte-derived signal to promote rapid, synergistic terminal differentiation in local myoblasts.
source: We therefore conclude that EphA7 acts non-cell-autonomously as a myocyte-derived signal to promote rapid, synergistic terminal differentiation in local myoblasts, consistent with observations of the community effect.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the rescue experiments with EphA7-Fc and the expression pattern of EphA7.

claim: In multiple contexts in vivo, EphA7 signals in reverse through ephrin-A5.
source: In multiple contexts in vivo, EphA7 signals in reverse through ephrin-A5 (Holmberg et al., 2000; Miller et al., 2006), and in an expression screen for all mammalian ephrins on WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells we noted that ephrin-A5 is present on cells of both strains but shows increased expression in EphA7-/- cells (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Holmberg et al., 2000; Miller et al., 2006.

claim: Ephrin-A5 is present on satellite cells of both WT and EphA7-/- strains but shows increased expression in EphA7-/- cells.
source: In multiple contexts in vivo, EphA7 signals in reverse through ephrin-A5 (Holmberg et al., 2000; Miller et al., 2006), and in an expression screen for all mammalian ephrins on WT and EphA7-/- satellite cells we noted that ephrin-A5 is present on cells of both strains but shows increased expression in EphA7-/- cells (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Upregulation of ephrin-A5 in EphA7-/- cells is consistent with upregulation of ephrin-A5 in other contexts in the EphA7-/- mouse.
source: This is consistent with upregulation of ephrin-A5 in other contexts in the EphA7-/- mouse (Miller et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Miller et al., 2006.

claim: EphA7KO C2C12 cells phenocopy primary myoblasts from EphA7-/- mice with lower levels of myogenin expression, fewer, smaller myotubes with fewer nuclei, and sustained proliferation even at high density.
source: Importantly, EphA7KO C2C12 cells phenocopy primary myoblasts from EphA7-/- mice with lower levels of myogenin expression, fewer, smaller myotubes with fewer nuclei, and sustained proliferation even at high density.
evidence: This statement is based on comparison of the phenotypes observed in EphA7KO C2C12 cells and primary EphA7-/- myoblasts.

claim: All three lines (unedited, EphA7KO, and ephrin-A5KO C2C12 cells) showed minimal expression of myogenin at low density on an unmodified laminin substrate.
source: While all three lines showed minimal expression of myogenin (indicating a lack of differentiation) at low density on an unmodified laminin substrate, unedited C2C12 cells increased their differentiation when grown at high density as would be predicted by the community effect, while EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells did not.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Unedited C2C12 cells increased their differentiation when grown at high density as would be predicted by the community effect, while EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells did not.
source: While all three lines showed minimal expression of myogenin (indicating a lack of differentiation) at low density on an unmodified laminin substrate, unedited C2C12 cells increased their differentiation when grown at high density as would be predicted by the community effect, while EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells did not.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Modifying the substrate with EphA7-Fc led to increased differentiation in both unedited and EphA7KO cells, even at low density and high serum.
source: In contrast, modifying the substrate with EphA7-Fc led to increased differentiation in both unedited and EphA7KO cells, even at low density and high serum, while differentiation in ephrin-A5KO cells was not rescued.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Differentiation in ephrin-A5KO cells was not rescued by EphA7-Fc.
source: In contrast, modifying the substrate with EphA7-Fc led to increased differentiation in both unedited and EphA7KO cells, even at low density and high serum, while differentiation in ephrin-A5KO cells was not rescued.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: When high density was combined with exposure to EphA7-Fc, differentiation by EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells was not significantly different from their response to EphA7-Fc at low densities.
source: When high density was combined with exposure to EphA7-Fc, differentiation by EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells was not significantly different from their response to EphA7-Fc at low densities, while unedited C2C12 cells showed even more enhanced differentiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Unedited C2C12 cells showed even more enhanced differentiation when high density was combined with exposure to EphA7-Fc.
source: When high density was combined with exposure to EphA7-Fc, differentiation by EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells was not significantly different from their response to EphA7-Fc at low densities, while unedited C2C12 cells showed even more enhanced differentiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Ephrin-A5 can transduce the EphA7 signal via recruitment of Fyn, a nonreceptor tyrosine kinase that activates downstream effectors such as Src, ERK, Rac, AKT, paxillin and p75.
source: One mechanism by which ephrin-A5 can transduce the EphA7 signal is via recruitment of Fyn, a nonreceptor tyrosine kinase that activates downstream effectors such as Src, ERK, Rac, AKT, paxillin and p75; in other cellular contexts this interaction regulates integrin-mediated signaling and adhesion, cell growth and survival, cytoskeletal remodeling, and cell motility (Holen et al., 2008; Lim et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Holen et al., 2008; Lim et al., 2008.

claim: In other cellular contexts, the Fyn interaction regulates integrin-mediated signaling and adhesion, cell growth and survival, cytoskeletal remodeling, and cell motility.
source: One mechanism by which ephrin-A5 can transduce the EphA7 signal is via recruitment of Fyn, a nonreceptor tyrosine kinase that activates downstream effectors such as Src, ERK, Rac, AKT, paxillin and p75; in other cellular contexts this interaction regulates integrin-mediated signaling and adhesion, cell growth and survival, cytoskeletal remodeling, and cell motility (Holen et al., 2008; Lim et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Holen et al., 2008; Lim et al., 2008.

claim: Unedited and EphA7KO C2C12 cells rapidly and robustly phosphorylated ERK1/2 in response to EphA7-Fc.
source: We found that unedited and EphA7KO C2C12 cells rapidly and robustly phosphorylated ERK1/2, but ephrin-A5KO C2C12 cells have significantly decreased phosphorylation after 10' of exposure to EphA7-Fc (Figure 8D).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Ephrin-A5KO C2C12 cells have significantly decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2 after 10' of exposure to EphA7-Fc.
source: We found that unedited and EphA7KO C2C12 cells rapidly and robustly phosphorylated ERK1/2, but ephrin-A5KO C2C12 cells have significantly decreased phosphorylation after 10' of exposure to EphA7-Fc (Figure 8D).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Ephrin-A5 is a strong candidate for the EphA7 receptor on myoblasts.
source: Based on these data, we conclude that ephrin-A5 is a strong candidate for the EphA7 receptor on myoblasts.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the rescue experiments, ERK phosphorylation data, and expression patterns.

claim: EphA7:ephrin-A5 interactions play a role in induction of terminal differentiation during skeletal muscle development and regeneration.
source: Taken together, these results support a role for EphA7:ephrin-A5 interactions in induction of terminal differentiation during skeletal muscle development and regeneration, and provide a novel molecular mechanism for the community effect.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined experimental findings throughout the manuscript.

claim: This study provides a novel molecular mechanism for the community effect.
source: Taken together, these results support a role for EphA7:ephrin-A5 interactions in induction of terminal differentiation during skeletal muscle development and regeneration, and provide a novel molecular mechanism for the community effect.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined experimental findings throughout the manuscript.

claim: This study is the first to identify a heterotypic, non-cell-autonomous signal between myogenic cells at distinct stages of differentiation.
source: While several other interactions mediating this effect have previously been described, we believe this study is the first to identify a heterotypic, non-cell-autonomous signal between myogenic cells at distinct stages of differentiation.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings relative to prior literature.

claim: The mechanism provides a way for rapidly amplifying the number of differentiated cells in a population once a sufficient local density has been reached and potential fusion partners are readily available.
source: As such, it provides a mechanism for rapidly amplifying the number of differentiated cells in a population once a sufficient local density has been reached and potential fusion partners are readily available.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the findings.

claim: Cells lacking ephrin-A5 show an even more pronounced failure to differentiate than those lacking EphA7.
source: Further, the observation that cells lacking ephrin-A5 show an even more pronounced failure to differentiate than those lacking EphA7 suggests the possibility that threshold levels of ephrin-A5 stimulation may be necessary to initiate even stochastic differentiation.
evidence: This observation is based on the data shown in Figure 8C comparing EphA7KO and ephrin-A5KO cells.

claim: Threshold levels of ephrin-A5 stimulation may be necessary to initiate even stochastic differentiation.
source: Further, the observation that cells lacking ephrin-A5 show an even more pronounced failure to differentiate than those lacking EphA7 suggests the possibility that threshold levels of ephrin-A5 stimulation may be necessary to initiate even stochastic differentiation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation that ephrin-A5KO cells have a more severe phenotype than EphA7KO cells.

claim: Skeletal muscle is unique among vertebrate somatic tissues in that skeletal myofibers are syncytial cells formed by fusion of hundreds or thousands of terminally-differentiated mononuclear cells.
source: Skeletal muscle is unique among vertebrate somatic tissues in that skeletal myofibers, the functional unit of the tissue, are syncytial cells formed by fusion of hundreds or thousands of terminally-differentiated mononuclear cells (myocytes).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field of muscle biology.

claim: Cell-cell contact and adhesion-based signals have been shown to be strongly promyogenic even in the presence of soluble factors that promote myoblast proliferation.
source: Indeed, cell-cell contact and adhesion-based signals have been shown to be strongly promyogenic even in the presence of soluble factors that promote myoblast proliferation and thereby inhibit myocyte differentiation.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field, as indicated by the review citations that follow.

claim: Adhesion proteins such as cadherins, their multifunctional coreceptors Cdo and Boc, and the netrin-3 receptor neogenin are necessary and sufficient to promote robust myogenesis in vitro and in vivo.
source: Adhesion proteins such as cadherins, their multifunctional coreceptors Cdo and Boc, and the netrin-3 receptor neogenin are necessary and sufficient to promote robust myogenesis in vitro and in vivo (reviewed in Krauss et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review by Krauss et al., 2005.

claim: The enhanced myogenesis brought about by juxtacrine interactions is distinct from promotion of myocyte fusion.
source: It is important to note that the enhanced myogenesis brought about by these juxtacrine interactions is distinct from promotion of myocyte fusion, which has recently been shown to require a class of proteins in vertebrate muscle that do not appear to be related to classical contact-mediated signaling (Millay et al., 2013; Quinn et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017), and instead appears to derive from upregulation of MyoD-dependent transcription (reviewed in Krauss et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Millay et al., 2013; Quinn et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017 and a review by Krauss et al., 2017.

claim: Myocyte fusion requires a class of proteins in vertebrate muscle that do not appear to be related to classical contact-mediated signaling.
source: It is important to note that the enhanced myogenesis brought about by these juxtacrine interactions is distinct from promotion of myocyte fusion, which has recently been shown to require a class of proteins in vertebrate muscle that do not appear to be related to classical contact-mediated signaling (Millay et al., 2013; Quinn et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017), and instead appears to derive from upregulation of MyoD-dependent transcription (reviewed in Krauss et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Millay et al., 2013; Quinn et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: Enhanced myogenesis from juxtacrine interactions appears to derive from upregulation of MyoD-dependent transcription.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review by Krauss et al., 2017.

claim: Interactions between Ephs and their ephrin ligands have been shown to directly affect differentiation in multiple contexts.
source: However, interactions between Ephs and their ephrin ligands have also been shown to directly affect differentiation: for example, EphB2:ephrinB1 interactions within the osteoblast lineage promote osteoblast differentiation by stimulating nuclear translocation of the transcriptional coactivator TAZ, and in multiple neuronal and stem cell lineages Eph/ephrin signaling modulates cell fate choice both directly and indirectly (reviewed in Wilkinson, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review by Wilkinson, 2014.

claim: EphB2:ephrinB1 interactions within the osteoblast lineage promote osteoblast differentiation by stimulating nuclear translocation of the transcriptional coactivator TAZ.

claim: EphA7 has been characterized as a tumor suppressor in several cancers.
source: EphA7 is a particularly likely candidate for a pro-differentiation molecule because it has been characterized as a tumor suppressor in several cancers (Wang et al., 2005; Nakanishi et al., 2007; Oricchio et al., 2011) as well as a negative regulator of proliferation through reverse signaling with ephrin-A2 in the adult stem cell niches of the hippocampus (Holmberg et al., 2005) and hair follicle (Genander et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2005; Nakanishi et al., 2007; Oricchio et al., 2011.

claim: EphA7 is a negative regulator of proliferation through reverse signaling with ephrin-A2 in the adult stem cell niches of the hippocampus.
source: EphA7 is a particularly likely candidate for a pro-differentiation molecule because it has been characterized as a tumor suppressor in several cancers (Wang et al., 2005; Nakanishi et al., 2007; Oricchio et al., 2011) as well as a negative regulator of proliferation through reverse signaling with ephrin-A2 in the adult stem cell niches of the hippocampus (Holmberg et al., 2005) and hair follicle (Genander et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Holmberg et al., 2005.

claim: EphA7 is a negative regulator of proliferation through reverse signaling with ephrin-A2 in the adult stem cell niche of the hair follicle.
source: EphA7 is a particularly likely candidate for a pro-differentiation molecule because it has been characterized as a tumor suppressor in several cancers (Wang et al., 2005; Nakanishi et al., 2007; Oricchio et al., 2011) as well as a negative regulator of proliferation through reverse signaling with ephrin-A2 in the adult stem cell niches of the hippocampus (Holmberg et al., 2005) and hair follicle (Genander et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Genander et al., 2010.

claim: Three different splice variants of EPHA7 have been identified, encoding one full length (FL) and two truncated (T1 and T2) proteins lacking the catalytic kinase domain.
source: Three different splice variants of EPHA7 have been identified, encoding one full length (FL) and two truncated (T1 and T2) proteins lacking the catalytic kinase domain (Holmberg et al., 2000), as have two splice variants of ephrin-A5 (one lacking an alternate exon) (Lai et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Holmberg et al., 2000.

claim: Two splice variants of ephrin-A5 have been identified (one lacking an alternate exon).
source: Three different splice variants of EPHA7 have been identified, encoding one full length (FL) and two truncated (T1 and T2) proteins lacking the catalytic kinase domain (Holmberg et al., 2000), as have two splice variants of ephrin-A5 (one lacking an alternate exon) (Lai et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lai et al., 1999.

claim: All three EphA7 proteins can signal in reverse via ephrin-A5.
source: All three EphA7 proteins can signal in reverse via ephrin-A5, and in some contexts such as the closing neural tube the switch from full-length to truncated (T1) EphA7 appears to mediate a switch from repulsive to adhesive interactions (Holmberg et al., 2000)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Holmberg et al., 2000.

claim: In the closing neural tube, the switch from full-length to truncated (T1) EphA7 appears to mediate a switch from repulsive to adhesive interactions.
source: All three EphA7 proteins can signal in reverse via ephrin-A5, and in some contexts such as the closing neural tube the switch from full-length to truncated (T1) EphA7 appears to mediate a switch from repulsive to adhesive interactions (Holmberg et al., 2000)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Holmberg et al., 2000.

claim: In the context of skeletal muscle regeneration, mRNA expression of all three variants of EphA7 and both variants of ephrin-A5 were detected.
source: In the context of skeletal muscle regeneration, we detected mRNA expression of all three variants of EphA7 and both variants of ephrin-A5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This statement is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: An initially small number of ephrin-A5+, EphA7- myoblasts will experience a combination of intrinsic and extrinsic factors that induce them to commit to differentiation, exit the cell cycle, and upregulate myogenin (stochastic commitment).
source: An initially small number of ephrin-A5+, EphA7- myoblasts will experience a combination of intrinsic and extrinsic factors that induce them to commit to differentiation, exit the cell cycle, and upregulate myogenin (stochastic commitment).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: Once myoblasts have committed to differentiation, these newly-differentiated myocytes will upregulate expression of EphA7.
source: Once this has occurred, these newly-differentiated myocytes will upregulate expression of EphA7, which will signal to adjacent ephrin-A5+ myoblasts via cell-cell contact and promote their differentiation (synergistic commitment).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings showing EphA7 expression on differentiated myocytes.

claim: EphA7 on newly-differentiated myocytes will signal to adjacent ephrin-A5+ myoblasts via cell-cell contact and promote their differentiation (synergistic commitment).
source: Once this has occurred, these newly-differentiated myocytes will upregulate expression of EphA7, which will signal to adjacent ephrin-A5+ myoblasts via cell-cell contact and promote their differentiation (synergistic commitment).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings showing non-cell-autonomous effects of EphA7.

claim: This rapidly differentiating population of adjacent cells can subsequently fuse into myotubes/myofibers to form the functional units of skeletal muscle.
source: This rapidly differentiating population of adjacent cells can subsequently fuse into myotubes/myofibers to form the functional units of skeletal muscle.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on established knowledge of muscle development.

claim: In the absence of EphA7, while stochastic commitment still occurs, synergistic commitment via the community effect is lost.
source: In the absence of EphA7, while stochastic commitment still occurs, synergistic commitment via the community effect is lost, leading to decreased numbers of myocytes available for fusion (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings in EphA7-/- mice and cells.

claim: Loss of synergistic commitment in the absence of EphA7 leads to decreased numbers of myocytes available for fusion.
source: In the absence of EphA7, while stochastic commitment still occurs, synergistic commitment via the community effect is lost, leading to decreased numbers of myocytes available for fusion (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the experimental findings showing reduced myofiber size and number in EphA7-/- mice.

claim: Both developmental and regenerative myogenesis still occurs in muscle lacking EphA7, but it progresses more slowly and produces smaller myofibers containing fewer myonuclei.
source: Thus, both developmental and regenerative myogenesis still occurs in muscle lacking EphA7, but it progresses more slowly and produces smaller myofibers containing fewer myonuclei.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings in EphA7-/- mice.

claim: Other molecules which promote specification to myogenesis by cell-cell contact act via upregulation of MyoD-dependent gene transcription.
source: Given that other molecules which promote specification to myogenesis by cell-cell contact act via upregulation of MyoD-dependent gene transcription, it is intriguing to speculate that upregulation of myogenin and commitment to terminal differentiation could be a direct consequence of EphA7 reverse signaling in myoblasts.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Upregulation of myogenin and commitment to terminal differentiation could be a direct consequence of EphA7 reverse signaling in myoblasts.
source: Given that other molecules which promote specification to myogenesis by cell-cell contact act via upregulation of MyoD-dependent gene transcription, it is intriguing to speculate that upregulation of myogenin and commitment to terminal differentiation could be a direct consequence of EphA7 reverse signaling in myoblasts.
